observations: Photo 0: a white games console in clear plastic wrap held up by a hand in a shop window; Xbox logo on the top; perforated vent grille over the top.
Photo 1: the same console at another angle; Xbox button logo on the front corner; grille and edges look clean under the wrap.
Body shape and grille pattern match the white Xbox One S family; no black circular fan vent, so not a Series S.
The front face is not shown straight on, so a disc slot can neither be seen nor ruled out.
No controller, power cable, HDMI lead or box shown; no underside label, rear ports or powered-on screen.
Shop setting with dealer branding and Jiji watermark.

identity.model: Xbox One S (All-Digital as claimed, front face not shown)
read_from: photo 1 Xbox button logo and One S body design

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show the Xbox logo and the One S white grille body.
The front face is not shown straight on, so the presence or absence of a disc slot cannot be confirmed.

claims.claim: Compact console (40% smaller than original Xbox One)
claims.evidence: This is a spec of the One S body seen in photos 0 and 1, not a condition claim.

claims.claim: Implied new or unused condition from the plastic wrap
claims.evidence: Plastic wrap in photos 0 and 1 does not prove it is unused or working.

risks.risk: Console may not power on or may have faults
risks.proof: Clip of the console booting to the home screen on a TV

risks.risk: No controller, power cable or HDMI lead included
risks.proof: Photo of everything included laid out next to the console
risks.if_unproven: as console only with no accessories

risks.risk: Console may be account-locked or banned from online services
risks.proof: Screenshot of the network settings showing a successful Xbox Live connection

risks.risk: Damaged or repaired rear ports or opened casing
risks.proof: Photo of the rear ports and the underside label with serial

proof_requests: Clip of the console powered on to the home screen on a TV
Straight-on photo of the front face and the underside label
response.reason: The Xbox logo and body design identify a white Xbox One S, and the claimed All-Digital edition is the lower-value variant, so it can be priced at its worst case as a not-working console only until a power-on clip and accessories are shown.
